title: Convoy TE-04, 3–4 May 1944
eyebrow: Luzon Strait · Coordinated attack group, Capt. G. E. Peterson

participants.name: PARCHE
participants.co: LCdr L. P. Ramage; pack commander Capt. G. E. Peterson aboard

paras.text: TINOSA found convoy TE-04 north of Luzon on the morning of 3 May and reported it to PARCHE and BANG; by the early hours of the 4th the three boats had attacked it in turn, and five of its six ships were gone. The boats' war patrol reports beside the escort division's record, on one GMT clock.
Japanese loss list: five ships, 30,542 GRT. Which boat sank which is still open; see the attack order in the log.
Yulin to Moji by way of Keelung, sailed 30 April with six ships; iron ore for Yawata (combinedfleet.com, secondary). Its ships are in the convoy's own record: [[convoy:te-04]].

Positions are the boats' own dead reckoning and star sights, and three navigators never quite agree, so the same convoy appears in slightly different places in each report. Lines between positions are straight; where a boat actually went in between is not recorded. Dashed outlines mark entries the report itself contradicts, kept with the reason.

BANG kept zone K (−10) and PARCHE zone I (−9); TINOSA kept zone H (−8) on station. Japanese records use Tokyo time (I, −9). On 29–30 April the target ship's own log and BANG's attack sheets agree to within one to seven minutes once both are in GMT.

War patrol reports, NARA microfilm M1752 (BANG 74802746, PARCHE 74828582, TINOSA 74856363). Nittatsu Maru's movement log and the 1st Surface Escort Division war diary via JACAR (National Institute for Defense Studies). Convoy lists and the 3–4 May sinking times from combinedfleet.com, a secondary source, flagged where used. Coastline: Natural Earth.

outcome.note: JANAC credits BANG with Kinrei Maru, but the secondary source's 0106 I for her sinking is the minute PARCHE fired her Attack 2. BANG fired at 0232 I, after PARCHE and TINOSA had scattered the convoy (her own words); the losses timed about 0300 (J15) are the nearer match

paras.text: Yulin to Moji, leaving Yulin on 30 April 1944 with six ships (April chart). The May chart draws the northbound track with two sinking marks and lists five ships sunk: 金嶺丸 昌竜丸 大翼丸 豊日丸 大武丸; the rest of the convoy is drawn into (基隆) Keelung for supplies (補給) and on to Moji. Six ships less five sunk leaves one survivor (inferred).

The chart's time and position beside the marks are faint: read 「4日 22?9」 N2?-46 E118-?4, low confidence; not paired with any one boat's attack. BANG, PARCHE and TINOSA attacked between the evening of the 3rd and the early hours of the 4th (engagement `luzon-strait-1944`, which weighs who sank which).
**Cargo: iron ore for Yawata** per combinedfleet.com (secondary); not in the escort division's record. The escorts are combinedfleet's; the April chart's escort cell can't be read with confidence.
The retired battle page listed a sixth ship, "Yulin", from combinedfleet.com; that is the port of departure, not a ship, and is left out. The sixth ship (the survivor) is not named in the record.
